text:
Maya: Heads-up — seeing slow but persistent memory growth on a few runtime boxes serving long-context chat workloads (~80k-120k token windows). Heap trending +12% over 24h for p99 load.
Jon: Yikes. Any profiling pointers?
Maya: Did a flame + allocation walk. Biggest hit is KV cache: many tiny freed slots left as tombstones, allocator ends up scattering live entries across many partially-used blocks -> high fragmentation.
Liam: Do you have numbers on fragile block counts / waste?
Maya: Quick paste from sampling: 
```
blocks_total: 12430
blocks_partial: 4821  # ~38.8%
avg_live_per_block: 3.1
wasted_bytes_est: 1.8GB
```
p99 resident went 5.4GB -> 6.2GB over 24h on that host.
Asha: Could this be long-context pinning (KV entries referenced by very long kv-keys) preventing compaction?
Maya: Partially. A subset of long-lived contexts continually append, leaving older prefixes tombstoned but still preventing full block reuse. Also observed that eviction policy prefers LRU at slice level which leaves micro-holes.
Jon: Did you try increasing block-size to reduce metadata overhead? e.g., move 512B->2KB?
Maya: We simulated. Larger block sizes reduce metadata overhead but increase internal waste per hole; with many small keys it made things worse. Best win seems to be smarter compaction + tombstone reclamation.
Liam: Outline of options: 1) aggressive background compaction (merge partial blocks, copy live entries into new contiguous blocks) 2) tombstone bitmap + quick reuse (mark holes reusable in-situ) 3) change eviction heuristic to avoid leaving <25% used blocks.
Maya: I sketched a compactor proto. Config: 
```
compactor.enabled = true
compactor.max_io_mb_per_sec = 20
compactor.block_fill_target = 0.85
compactor.tombstone_threshold = 0.15
```
Behavior: scan partial blocks, copy live entries into new blocks until fill target reached, atomically swap, free old block. Background/cancellable.
Asha: Sounds reasonable. Risk is write amplification during heavy write bursts. Need throttling + low-priority scheduling.
Jon: Also think about cheap fast path: ephemeral tombstone reuse — when allocating, prefer carving into blocks with tombstone fraction > X and reclaim slots without a full copy. That avoids copy cost but complicates allocator invariants.
Maya: Agreed. I added a hybrid plan: prefer tombstone-reuse for small allocations (<256B) and compactor for bigger objects.
infra-bot: perf test job queued: kv-frag/scrub-proto-4942008765 on staging (will run on 4 hosts).
Jon: For experiments we should A/B: baseline vs tombstone-reuse vs full compaction. Capture p95/p99 resident, allocation churn, token-latency impact.
Liam: Also instrument kernel-selection/batching interaction: compaction runs could increase CPU and affect batched decoding latency. Need to measure decode tail latency during compaction.
Maya: Good call. I'll add a tracer that correlates compactor windows with inference tail latency.
Asha: Can we make compactor idempotent and safe across concurrent instances? We have multiple runtime shards per host.
Maya: Plan: compactor uses block-level CAS and per-shard lease. If CAS fails, we skip block. That keeps it safe.
Jon: Who will own the first run and PR?
Maya: I'll draft the PR and a small in-staging job. Jon, can you run the perf job and collect traces?
Jon: Yep, I'll kick it off after lunch.
Maya: Thanks. If this reduces wasted_bytes by >50% we're probably good to roll to prod canary. Otherwise iterate. :thumbsup:
Asha: One more ask — add an emergency toggle to disable compactor if we see decode latency regressions.
Maya: Will include a runtime flag and metric 'compactor.phase' so ops can toggle.
Jon: Cool. I'll post perf results once infra-bot finishes. :rocket:
